caption:
357 identical paired-A events; 194 event families. Potency comes from existing S-wave spectra and the Haenam Kim & Kim (1983), Vp/Vs=1.73.
Both models and magnitude conventions are retained in the tables. Shading resamples whole families; the published Liu curve is not shifted.

Red dotted: Liu c=0.040. Positive RMSE gain favors the quadratic; error bars resample paired held-out family losses.
Binned quadratic gains are relative to binned linear fits. Across the full sample, the ordinary family-weighted line predicts at least as well.
Hong panel: final group independently restricts the full catalog ML range; it is not the next nested selection.

Left: ΔMP=ΔMw/3 follows algebraically from P0=M0/(ρVs²) and M0∝ρVs³ in this analytical S-wave method.
It is not an independent validation of full-waveform Mpv. Right: attenuation/distance definitions differ even at identical amplitude.
The Korean relation uses epicentral distance; Liu supplement S1 uses Hutton–Boore with hypocentral distance.

357 identical paired-A events; 194 families. Mw uses C=9.05 and the Haenam Kim & Kim (1983) source model.
The fit weights, bootstrap blocks, bins and prediction tests match the potency analysis. Shading resamples whole families.
These are selected-sample relations; the published Liu potency curve is not a moment-magnitude calibration.

Six events with measured ML > 4, in five independent families. Dates are UTC. Events 2 and 3 are in the Gyeongju family.
The quadratic improves large-event prediction, while changes below ML 4 are small. The five-family gain interval includes zero.
The highest event is outside the training magnitude range when its entire family is held out. KMA ML > 4 gives only three events.

357 paired-A events. Right: remove the ML polynomial estimated jointly with depth; the remaining slope is conditional on ML.
Shading: 95% whole-family coefficient intervals. Diamonds: 5-km-bin medians. Dotted: Kim & Kim boundary at 15 km.
The decline is concentrated at 5–15 km; a slope within the 15–24 km subset is unresolved. Depth is not established as the cause.
